I am a 50-year-old farmer in Quzhou County, Hebei. I have worked my 7 mu for 35 years. My wife and I do all the labor ourselves. We have a well, so I can irrigate when the rains are not enough. I only finished primary school, but I know this land better than any book.

This year I will plant 4 mu of chili in the spring. Chili is my main cash crop, and the dealers in town pay good money for it. I will buy hybrid chili seeds from the seed shop because they yield more and the peppers look better. I will rotary till the fields and put down compound fertilizer as a base. When the plants start flowering, I will top-dress with urea. The chili will need six irrigations from May to September and five pesticide sprays for the aphids and mites that always come in summer.

After I pull the chili out in September and October, I will plant autumn cabbage on those same 4 mu. The cool weather is good for cabbage. I will use hybrid cabbage seeds. Cabbage needs plenty of food but not as much nitrogen as chili. I will irrigate five times and spray pesticides four times to keep the caterpillars off.

I keep 2 mu for summer maize. I need the grain for flour and the stalks for fuel and fodder. I will plant improved maize seed. It is easy to manage—only three irrigations and two pesticide sprays.

The remaining 1 mu I use for spinach. I sow it in early spring and again in late autumn for winter harvest. Spinach brings quick money and is good for our table. I use traditional spinach seeds. It does not need much fertilizer—just some compost and a little urea—and I irrigate three or four times with two sprays.

I watch the sky and the soil. I have done this long enough to know when to plant and when to water. I do not follow books; I follow what I have seen work.
